svg.title: Unconditional incompatible latch requests queue on the BCB and are granted one zero-crossing at a time
svg.desc: A BCB holds an atomic latch tuple with mode WRITE, fix count one, and the waiter-exists bit set. One hundred unconditional WRITE requesters are appended to the BCB wait queue in arrival order; a blocking promoter is inserted at the head. Each waiter sleeps with a timed wait and honours interrupts. When the holder unfixes and the fix count reaches zero, the releasing thread walks the queue from the head. It removes entries that already gave up and leaves flush waiters in place. If it grants a READ, it continues scanning, leaves incompatible WRITE entries queued, and grants later READ entries. If it grants a WRITE, the latch becomes WRITE and the scan stops. The waker updates the latch tuple; each woken waiter records its own holder. Outcomes are grant, timeout treated as a deadlock victim, or interrupt with removal and no debt. This is a serialized handoff, not a fairness theorem.
svg.text: One hundred unconditional WRITE requests on one latched page
next_wait_thrd: head of the wait queue
a blocking promoter is inserted at the head instead of the tail
every waiter sleeps with a timed wait bounded by page_latch_timeout_in_msecs and honours interrupts
Holder unfixes, fcnt reaches 0, latch mode becomes NO_LATCH: the releasing thread walks the queue from the head
1. Skip entries that already gave up: their request mode was reset to NO_LATCH by timeout or interrupt.
2. Leave FLUSH waiters in place; they are woken by flush completion, not by unfix.
3. First grant is READ: scan onward, keep writers queued, grant later readers. First grant is WRITE: grant it and stop.
4. The waker sets the new latch mode and adds the waiter's requested fix count; the woken waiter only records its own holder.
5. If blocked readers or writers remain, waiter_exists stays set so newcomers keep queueing instead of barging.
Latch, global fcnt, and this thread's holder
are set: one fix debt, the same postcondition
Timeout: treated as a deadlock victim
The request ends without a fix debt.
The thread removes itself from the queue
and returns an error: no page pointer,
One hundred writers are served one grant per zero-crossing. Holder re-entry, promoters at the head, and reader grouping can reorder service,
so this is a serialized handoff, not a fairness theorem. Strict FIFO, starvation freedom, and exact timing are not established by the source.
